feedback:
Written before this candidate races. Evidence from earlier iterations: iteration 2 (16 mm, x = ±0.05 m, y 0.04, kp 3.5) is the best pairing at 26.9949 with zero line loss on oval and slalom. Iteration 1 showed span removes line loss. Iterations 2 to 6 showed max_error stays at about 0.061 m under footprint change (2), kp 3.0 to 4.4 (2, 4), wheel_track 0.15 (4), mass 0.6 (5) and y 0.02 to 0.06 (3, 6). Iteration 6 (y 0.02) scored the same as iteration 2, so the y = 0.02 test you proposed has already been run and did not move the excursion.

Wheel radius is a sound lever to test, because it raises the speed per wheel rotation. It also raises yaw per unit of PWM difference by about 33 percent, since yaw is wheel-speed difference over wheel_track. I have scaled kp to 2.6 to keep the effective steering gain at the iteration-2 level, so any change in max_error reflects the geometry. I make no prediction of this robot's result.

What to do next depends on the race. If max_error stays at about 0.061 m with line loss at zero, the excursion is not speed or radius, and geometry alone has not removed it. In that case, hold the current row and test the one lever no iteration has tried, a narrower wheel_track. If line loss returns at 0.04 m radius, hold radius at 0.03 m and keep the iteration-2 row.
requested_changes: Keep the iteration-2 row (16 mm, x = ±0.05 m, y 0.04 m, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m) and test wheel_radius 0.04 m as the single change; report max_error and line_loss_events per track.
If max_error stays at about 0.061 m with line loss at zero, try wheel_track 0.10 m (narrower, more yaw per PWM difference) on the 0.04 m radius, since wheel_track has only been tested at 0.15 m.
If line loss returns at 0.04 m radius, revert radius to 0.03 m and hold the iteration-2 row, since no tested change has improved on it.
